subject: POC success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:00:00Z
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments

Thanks again for the call today, Priya - great discussion on the integration and evaluation priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC.

1) Proposed success criteria / KPIs (what we agreed to discuss):
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 150 ms for the checkout flow (measured end-to-end from request to token returned).
- Throughput: sustain 300 requests/sec for peak window; burst to 500 req/sec for short peaks (under 5 minutes) without errors.
- Cost: target operational cost <= $0.0006 per token (applies to gen path + embeddings used for enrichment).
- Quality: intent recognition accuracy >= 95% on your test-suite (we'll run the evaluation harness against your labeled set).

2) Evaluation plan / measurement:
- Redwood will run a mixed workload with your sample traffic and our load generator; we'll provide the harness and scripts.
- Quality will be measured via the shared test-suite (we'll accept CSV annotated with ground-truth labels).
- We will capture both service metrics (p95, p99, errors) and token-level costs using our billing tracer.

3) Timeline:
- Provide sample traffic + test-suite by +2026-10-12 (action: Atlas).
- Kickoff/tech sync: week of 2026-10-18 (action: Redwood + Atlas).
- POC run window: 2 weeks from kickoff (expected completion by 2026-11-01).

4) Ownership:
- Redwood: Jordan (sales) - program lead; Dev (SE) - technical lead / test harness; Marissa (CS) - onboarding & success manager.
- Atlas: Priya - product owner; engineering contact TBD (please cc when confirmed).

5) Next steps (short):
- Priya to confirm sample traffic & preferred kickoff dates by 2026-10-09.
- Jordan to share POC SOW and evaluation plan (attached).

Attachments: POC-SOW-v1.pdf (scope & SOW).
Shared doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2B3C-Atlas-POC-KPIs

Thanks - looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T17:10:00Z
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments

Thanks Jordan - thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications/questions from our side: 

- Latency: Can we measure p95 both at service edge (our ingress) and at Redwood's inference endpoint? For our SLA, p95 end-to-end < 150 ms is ideal. If needed we can accept p95 inference < 120 ms.
- Throughput: 300 req/sec steady is fine; we do expect occasional batch settlements that could create short bursts up to ~450 req/sec. Can Redwood support 450 as an upper bound?
- Cost: Our procurement prefers < $0.0005/token if possible - any levers you recommend (quantization, batching profiles) to hit that?
- Quality: We'll share a 1k-item labeled test set by 10/12. We need an evaluation script that outputs precision/recall and a confusion matrix.

We're generally aligned on timeline. We can do kickoff the week of 10/18 - prefer 10/19 or 10/20. Also please include in the SOW a short paragraph about data handling and retention for the POC (SOC2 requirements).

I'll send sample traffic files by 10/12.

Priya Sharma
Head of Product - Risk & Checkout
Atlas Payments
priya.sharma@atlaspayments.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments

Appreciate the quick reply, Priya - responses inline below and an updated plan.

- Latency measurement: yes, we'll capture both edge (your ingress) and inference endpoint p95/p99. For the POC acceptance we'll use end-to-end p95 < 150 ms as the primary gate; inference p95 target 120 ms is a helpful internal goal.
- Throughput: Redwood will size the test to sustain 300 req/sec and validate bursts up to 500 req/sec for 5 min windows. We'll capture error rates and latency during burst windows.
- Cost levers: quantization + aggressive batching can get you near $0.00048/token in our benchmarks - Dev will propose a profile after we see sample traffic.
- Quality evaluation: we'll provide an evaluation script that outputs precision/recall and a confusion matrix; please confirm your label format (CSV with columns: id, input, expected_label).

Updated timeline and owners:
- 10/12: Atlas provides sample traffic + labeled test-suite. (Priya)
- 10/14: Redwood shares evaluation harness & loadgen config (Dev).
- 10/19: Kickoff tech sync (calendar invite pending).
- 10/19-11/02: POC run window.

I've attached the evaluation-plan.xlsx with a proposed test matrix and acceptance gates.

Next steps for Priya: confirm label CSV format and preferred kickoff date (10/19 vs 10/20).

Thanks,
Jordan

Hi all - quick technical note on measuring latency/cost for the POC and what we'll need from Atlas: 

Plan:
- We'll run a controlled test using our load generator (open-source harness) that replays your sample requests with timing preserved. We'll attach a short loadgen-config.yaml and the harness scripts.
- Measurement points: client-side (replay), edge (if you want us to deploy a tiny probe), and inference endpoint. We'll instrument traces and correlate with request IDs you provide.
- Cost/token measurement: we will enable billing traces which annotate tokens generated and compute cost with the quantization profile applied. This will give you per-run cost estimates.

What we need from Atlas:
- Representative sample of requests (anonymized) and the labeled test-suite (CSV).
- Expected traffic distribution across paths (checkout, auth, enrichment).
- Any IPs to whitelist for load generator.

I attached loadgen-config.yaml (stub) and a short README. Once we receive samples I'll run a quick dry-run targeting 1000 req/sec locally to sanity-check configs before the POC run.

Dev
